1.text:
3x = 18y - 45

One of the two equations in a system of linear equations is given. The system has no solution. Which equation could be the second equation in this system?
1.showWork: Divide the given equation by 3: x = 6y − 15. For no solution, the second equation must have the same slope but a different intercept. (1/3)x = 2y ⇒ x = 6y, which is parallel to x = 6y − 15 and distinct, so no solution.

2.text: In the xy-plane, lines k and j are perpendicular and intersect at the point (5, 26). Line j passes through the origin, and line k passes through the point (p, 0), where p is a constant. What is the value of p?

3.text: In 2010, a skating team had a total of 34 skaters, each classified as either advanced or intermediate. From 2010 to 2020, the number of advanced skaters on the team increased by approximately 67%, and the number of intermediate skaters on the team increased by approximately 44%. The total number of skaters on the team increased by approximately 56%. Which equation best represents this situation, where a represents the number of advanced skaters on the team in 2010 and b represents the number of intermediate skaters on the team in 2010?
3.showWork: Advanced become 1.67a; intermediate become 1.44b; total becomes 34(1.56). So 1.67a + 1.44b = 34(1.56).

4.text: For a survey, a sample of 562 people was selected at random from all registered voters in a county. Based on the survey, it is estimated that 73% of all registered voters in the county are in favor of a new law, with an associated margin of error of 3.67%. Which of the following best describes the plausible values for the percent of all registered voters in the county who are in favor of the new law?

choices.A: Any value greater than 69.33% and less than 76.67%
choices.B: Any value less than 69.33% or greater than 76.67%

4.showWork: Plausible values are within the margin of error: 73% ± 3.67% → between 69.33% and 76.67%.

6.text:
h(x) = (1/2)(x)(83)

The given function h represents the area, in square inches, of a triangle with a base of x inches and a fixed height. What is the height, in inches, of the triangle?
6.showWork: Area = (1/2)·base·height = (1/2)·x·83, so the fixed height is 83.

7.text:
y - x = 16
y = x² - 14x

The graphs of the equations in the given system intersect at the point (x, y) in the xy-plane. What is a possible value of y?
7.showWork: From the first equation, y = x + 16. Substitute: x + 16 = x² − 14x ⇒ x² − 15x − 16 = 0 ⇒ (x − 16)(x + 1) = 0. When x = 16, y = 32.

8.text: An object travels x inches in y seconds. At this rate, which expression represents the time, in seconds, it takes the object to travel a distance of 29x inches?
8.showWork: Rate is x/y inches per second. Time for 29x inches is (29x)/(x/y) = 29y.

9.text: The function g is defined by g(x) = 27 - x. What is the value of g(3)?

10.text: Micah deposited a total of $3,600 into two retirement accounts last year by depositing x dollars once each month into one account and y dollars twice each month into the other account. Which equation represents this situation?
10.showWork: Once each month for 12 months: 12x. Twice each month: 24y. Total: 12x + 24y = 3,600.

11.text: The ratio 10 to 3 is equivalent to the ratio 40 to 3k, where k is a constant. What is the value of k?

15.text: If ((1/2)x - 23/2)² - 81 = 0, what is the value of (x - 23)²?

16.text: Rectangles ABCD and EFGH are similar. The length of each side of EFGH is 7 times the length of the corresponding side of ABCD. The area of ABCD is 84 square units. What is the area, in square units, of EFGH?
16.showWork: Area scale factor is 7² = 49. Area of EFGH = 84 × 49 = 4,116.

17.text: On a plot of land, 48.0% of the square footage is farmland and the remaining square footage is pasture. There are buildings on exactly 28.5% of the square footage of the farmland, and there are buildings on exactly 11.0% of the square footage of the pasture. If there are buildings on exactly p% of the square footage of the plot of land, what is the value of p?

18.text:
The scatterplot shows data set A, which consists of the weights y, in pounds, of a Labrador retriever puppy at various ages, x, in months. The equation of a line of best fit for the relationship in data set A can be written as y = -5.0 + 8.7x, where 2 ≤ x ≤ 6.

The puppy was weighed again at 9 months old and weighed 52 pounds. Data set B consists of all the data points in data set A as well as the data point (9, 52). The equation of a line of best fit for data set B can be written as y = r + sx, where r and s are constants and 2 ≤ x ≤ 9. Assuming the equations of the lines of best fit are calculated in the same way, which of the following is the best estimate for the value of s?
18.figure: Scatterplot first quadrant. x-axis 0–10 labeled every 1; y-axis 0–60 labeled every 10; origin O. Five filled points approx (2,12), (3,22), (4,28), (5,41), (6,46). No trend line drawn.
18.showWork: Original slope ≈ 8.7. New point (9,52) lies well below the old line’s prediction (−5 + 8.7·9 ≈ 73.3), so the new best-fit slope decreases; 5.8 is the only smaller plausible estimate.

19.text: A book-of-the-month club charges $17 for the first book purchased during the month and an additional $13 for each book after the first. Which equation describes this situation, where y is the total cost, in dollars, for books purchased during a month, x is the number of books purchased during the month, and x > 0?
19.showWork: First book $17 plus $13 for each of the remaining (x − 1) books: y = 13(x − 1) + 17.

20.text: A company developed a plan to set the selling price of a product. The company determined that for a selling price of $120.00, zero products would be sold. For each $1.50 decrease in the selling price, the number of products sold would increase by one. For a revenue of exactly $1,966.50, which of the following could be the number of products sold? (revenue = price × number of products sold)

y = 4x² - bx - 5

Which of the following equations is equivalent to the given equation, where b is a positive constant?

23.text: The equation d = 6t + 270 gives the distance d, in feet, from a reference point on the surface of Mars to a Mars rover, where t is the number of minutes after the start of a period of observation. By how many feet does the Mars rover's distance from the reference point increase over a period of 20 minutes?
23.showWork: Distance increases by 6 feet per minute, so in 20 minutes: 6 × 20 = 120 feet.

24.text: A line intersects two parallel lines, forming four acute angles and four obtuse angles. The measure of one of the acute angles is (9x - 650)°. The sum of the measures of one of the acute angles and three of the obtuse angles is (-18x + w)°. What is the value of w?
24.showWork: Each obtuse angle is 180° − acute. Acute + 3·obtuse = acute + 3(180 − acute) = 540 − 2·acute = 540 − 2(9x − 650) = 1840 − 18x. So w = 1840.
